4-0-gpa.title: Is a 4.0 GPA good?
4-0-gpa.content: Yes. A 4.0 is an excellent GPA, well above the national average of about 3.1. It shows consistent A work and is competitive for selective colleges, honors programs and merit scholarships.

4-0-gpa.title: What letter grade and percentage is a 4.0 GPA?
4-0-gpa.content: A 4.0 GPA is an A average on the standard unweighted 4.0 scale, which is 93–100%. Schools set their own cutoffs, so check how your school converts percentages to grade points.

4-0-gpa.title: Can I get into college with a 4.0 GPA?
4-0-gpa.content: Yes. A 4.0 makes you competitive at most colleges, including many selective ones. At the most selective schools a high GPA is expected, so course rigor, essays, recommendations and activities decide between strong applicants.

4-0-gpa.title: Can you have a GPA higher than 4.0?
4-0-gpa.content: Yes, on a weighted scale. Many schools add extra points for Honors, AP or IB classes, so an A in a weighted class can count as more than 4.0. On the unweighted scale, 4.0 is the top.

4-0-gpa.title: How do I keep a 4.0 GPA?
4-0-gpa.content: Any grade below an A lowers a 4.0, so protect every class: plan study time around your hardest courses, ask for help as soon as something doesn't click, and aim above the A cutoff so one weak test doesn't drop the grade.

4-0-gpa.title: Is a 4.0 unweighted better than a higher weighted GPA?
4-0-gpa.content: Neither is automatically better. Colleges look at both the grades and how hard the classes were, and many recalculate GPAs their own way. A 4.0 in demanding courses is the strongest combination.

3-9-gpa.content: Yes. A 3.9 clears the minimum GPA for most merit scholarships, which makes the rest of the application (essays, activities, test scores where required) the deciding factor.

1-0-gpa.title: Is a 1.0 weighted GPA the same as a 1.0 unweighted GPA?
1-0-gpa.content: No. A 1.0 weighted GPA includes extra points for Honors, AP or IB classes, so the unweighted GPA behind it is lower: with a quarter of your classes AP at +1.0, it works out to about a 0.75 unweighted. Open “Is your 1.0 weighted?” on this page to estimate yours from your own classes.

1-0-gpa.title: How can I raise a 1.0 GPA to a 2.0?
1-0-gpa.content: With A's in your next classes. If you have finished 8 equal-credit classes, about 4 more A's take a 1.0 to a 2.0; after 16 classes it takes about 8. The earlier you start, the faster it moves, so focus first on the classes closest to the next grade up.

1-0-gpa.title: Can I graduate high school with a 1.0 GPA?
1-0-gpa.content: Usually, yes, as long as you pass the classes and earn the credits your state and school require; a D is a passing grade at most schools. Some schools set a minimum GPA for sports or activities, so check your school's policy and talk to your counselor.
